actions.action: Inspect leaf undersides and joints for pests with a magnifier or phone zoom
Remove affected leaves and dispose of them away from other plants
Test diluted ACV spray on one leaf first
Lightly spray diluted ACV (1 tbsp per quart)
If spots keep spreading, apply copper-based fungicide or neem oil
Trim mushy, brown or smelly roots if present
Repot in fresh fast-draining aroid mix with perlite or orchid bark
Check that top 2-3 inches of soil are dry before watering, then water at the soil
Improve airflow and space plant away from others
Isolate the plant from other houseplants
Monitor for new spots over 2-3 weeks
If spots persist, get a closer look or second opinion

reason: The answer names fungal leaf spot as the most likely cause and suggests removing leaves, but the copper fungicide that fixed it is only a conditional fallback behind ACV spray. Nothing it recommends is likely to harm the plant.
